newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 24.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* IBM reported quarterly profits which were ahead of expectations and put forth an optimistic outlook for the remainder of the year.
* Hewlett-Packard announced plans to buy VeriFone in a stock swap valued at $1.18 billion. VeriFone makes credit card authorization products.
* Quaker Oats said its chief executive officer William Smithburg would resign and reported a $1.11 billion quarterly loss.
* The International Monetary Fund said it expected world-wide output to grow 4.4 percent in 1997 and 1998, up from four percent from last year.
* Sunbeam reported quarterly earnings which were ahead of forecasts, suggesting the company's restructuring may have produced some results.
* The Dow Jones industrials closed down 20.87 points at 6,812.72, following Tuesday's large point-gain.
* At the General Electric annual meeting, CEO John Welch defended himself against criticism of his pay package and said the company's quality program was having an effect.
* Walt Disney posted better-than-expected pro-forma quarterly earnings, helped by better theme park attendance and profitable films.
* Netscape posted profits which beat projections, helped by corporate sales growth.
* According to I/B/E/S, first quarter earnings so far make it look as if this will be the seventeenth quarter in which results have beaten expectations.

* The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission accused Joseph Jett, the former head of government bonds at Kidder, of introducing allegedly bogus diary entries in an SEC trial over his role in a trading scandal.
* Pharmacia & Upjohn said its earnings would fall well below estimates and its shares fell 13.6 percent.
* The latest U.S. wireless auction is not going that well, helping television broadcasters' attempts to scrap auctioning some of their airwave rights.
* Shares of Bre-X gained as investors attempted to work through details of the developments surrounding the Busang gold field in Indonesia.

* Heard on the Street: Two days ago, in a talk aimed at calming employees of Viacom's faltering Blockbuster video rental division, Viacom Chairman Sumner Redstone said, "Those of you who just joined the organization must be wondering just what you've gotten yourselves into." Shareholders could be forgiven for wondering the same thing.
* Credit markets: The bond market retreated yesterday despite a favorable sale of five-year Treasury securities as disappointment over events in Washington and other factors spurred a sell-off.
